title: Son accused of attacking mother dies
article: Montreal police are investigating the death of a man accused of breaking into his mother's home last month and trying to stab her to death.

The body of 42-year-old John Burke was found just as a warrant for his arrest was being prepared for missing a court appearance. He had fallen 17 stories to his death. Burke was arrested April 1 and charged in the attempted murder of his mother.

Maria Ines Llamas, 68, was left for dead on the basement stairs of her home on March 17. She had been sprayed with pepper spray, beaten and stabbed repeatedly in the chest, neck and shoulder by a masked assailant. Police arrested Burke after a footprint was taken on eye glasses knocked off his mother during the attack.

Burke's mother says the justice system failed her son and is to blame for his death. Her anger is stronger than her grief. Llama says, "I am very sad. Not only for myself. But I'm very angry at the system. What the judge did. Or what he failed to do."

Police and the crown wanted Burke to stay in jail .The judge disagreed and released him on bail. His mother says, "He should not be out in the streets. Which is dangerous for anybody. It's dangerous for us. But it's dangerous for himself."

Proof of that came when he jumped 17 floors to his death. His mother doesn't think it's really a suicide."It's almost like he's been murdered. He's he was pushed to do what he did somehow. He was cornered."

Llamas blames the judge for releasing a man who needed help. But Burke's lawyer, Jeffrey Boro, says the judge was simply following the law, because Burke had no criminal record or psychological problems and there was no reason to keep him. The crown was going to appeal that decision to release him, just before Burke died.
